text: Nystatin, a polyene antifungal, has been identified as a potential inhibitor of the MEK1 (MAP2K1) kinase, a critical node in the MAPK/ERK signaling pathway frequently hyperactivated in melanoma. Molecular docking studies suggest that Nystatin binds to the ATP-binding pocket of MAP2K1, effectively stabilizing the kinase in an inactive conformation and disrupting the downstream phosphorylation of ERK1/2. By inhibiting this oncogenic signaling cascade, Nystatin suppresses the proliferation and survival of BRAF-mutant melanoma cells, offering a potential repurposing strategy to overcome resistance to conventional BRAF inhibitors.
